# contentful_app_installation (Resource)

Installs a Contentful app in an environment and manages its installation parameters.

## Example Usage

Terraform shows changes to `refreshInterval` in the plan while it redacts `apiKey`, which the example supplies through a sensitive variable. The [App Definition example](app_definition#example-usage) declares both parameters. Restrict access to state and saved plans.

```terraform
# The custom and Marketplace examples install two different apps.
# Use existing App Definition IDs and the agreements required by the Marketplace app.
resource "contentful_app_installation" "custom" {
  space_id       = var.contentful_space_id
  environment_id = var.contentful_environment_id

  app_definition_id = var.app_definition_id

  parameters = {
    refreshInterval = jsonencode(30)
    apiKey          = jsonencode(var.app_api_key)
  }
}

resource "contentful_app_installation" "marketplace" {
  space_id       = var.contentful_space_id
  environment_id = var.contentful_environment_id

  app_definition_id = var.marketplace_app_definition_id

  marketplace = [
    "i-accept-end-user-license-agreement",
    "i-accept-marketplace-terms-of-service",
    "i-accept-privacy-policy",
  ]
}
```

## Updating parameters

Changing a parameter or a `marketplace` acknowledgment sends every parameter in the plan to Contentful, including keys listed in `ignore_changes`. A write can overwrite edits made since refresh. It can restore an externally rotated secret even when the plan shows no change to that key. See [App Installation secrets](../guides/secrets-and-state#app-installation-secrets).

Omitting a key from the planned map can remove that parameter, including an optional Secret. An empty map sends `{}`, which Contentful can reject if the app requires a parameter. A null map omits the entire parameter object and can clear existing values. To send a JSON null, use `jsonencode(null)`. Contentful rejects JSON null for a declared Secret. A bare Terraform null at a key is invalid.

## Upgrading from the single JSON string

Replace `parameters = jsonencode(local.settings)` with `parameters = { for id, value in local.settings : id => jsonencode(value) }`. If `local.settings` can be null, use `local.settings == null ? null : { for id, value in local.settings : id => jsonencode(value) }`.

If you plan to add `ignore_changes` for a sensitive parameter, first apply the map configuration with that key supplied by its sensitive variable. This lets Terraform record sensitivity for the individual key before you ignore changes to it.

A module output that returns `parameters` directly changes from a JSON string to a map of JSON-encoded strings, even when the installation has no planned changes. If `local.params` refers to `contentful_app_installation.custom.parameters`, use `jsondecode(local.params["editor"])` for one key, or `local.params == null ? null : { for id, encoded in local.params : id => jsondecode(encoded) }` for the whole object.

Terraform upgrades saved state locally. With equivalent values and no remote drift, the upgrade requires no PUT. JSON formatting alone can still produce a local state change. An omitted or JSON `null` document becomes a null map. An empty object stays empty, and a key whose value is JSON `null` retains that value.

The upgrade stops if the saved document is invalid JSON, has a root other than an object or null, or contains a parameter ID Terraform would change during Unicode normalization. If Contentful holds representable parameters and the previous provider can read the saved state, review and apply a refresh-only plan with the previous provider and configuration.

If refresh cannot read the old state, back it up before removing the old state binding and importing the existing installation with the new provider. Correct any unrepresentable remote parameters before import. Keep a compatible state snapshot if you need to roll back.

## Schema

### Required

- `app_definition_id` (String) ID of the app definition being installed. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment where the app is installed. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `space_id` (String) ID of the space where the app is installed. Changing this value replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `marketplace` (Set of String) Marketplace agreement acknowledgments sent to Contentful when installing the app. Defaults to an empty set. Use the acknowledgment strings required by the selected Marketplace app.
- `parameters` (Map of String) Installation parameters keyed by parameter ID. Use `jsonencode` for each value. See [Updating parameters](#updating-parameters) for the effects of omitting or ignoring a key.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite Terraform resource identifier in `space_id/environment_id/app_definition_id` form.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Duration for the complete operation, including retries, for example `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.
- `delete` (String) Includes retries and uses the duration saved in state (default `2m`, minimum provider timeout `10s`).
- `read` (String) Includes retries and uses the duration saved in state (default `2m`, minimum provider timeout `10s`).
- `update` (String) Duration for the complete operation, including retries, for example `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.

## Import

Import records the values Contentful returns, including any masks. Before applying changes, configure the values you want Terraform to manage.

### By identity (Terraform 1.12 or later)

```terraform
import {
  identity = {
    space_id          = var.contentful_space_id
    environment_id    = var.contentful_environment_id
    app_definition_id = var.app_definition_id
  }
  to = contentful_app_installation.custom
}
```

### By ID (Terraform 1.5 or later)

```terraform
import {
  id = "${var.contentful_space_id}/${var.contentful_environment_id}/${var.app_definition_id}"
  to = contentful_app_installation.custom
}
```

### From the command line

```shell
terraform import contentful_app_installation.custom "$CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID/$CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID/$CONTENTFUL_APP_DEFINITION_ID"
```
